laws.rule: A park pass is required to visit Kakadu National Park and is valid for 7 days. Parks Australia prices vary by season. In the dry season (15 May to 31 October) an adult (16 years and over) pass is A$40, a child (aged 5 to 15) A$20, a family (2 adults and 2 or more children) A$100 and a concession pass A$30. In the tropical summer (1 November to 14 May) those prices are A$25, A$12.50, A$65 and A$19. Park passes are free for Northern Territory residents. The same official page says passes purchased to visit the park between 1 July and 31 October 2026 will be charged at the tropical-summer rates. You can buy a pass online or at listed outlets including the Bowali Visitor Centre. An additional permit may be needed for research, filming, overnight bushwalking or camping outside designated areas.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: The park's Traditional Owners welcome visitors. Aboriginal people are called Bininj in the north of the park and Mungguy in the south. They may expect a 'hello' from non-Aboriginal visitors, though they do not traditionally greet each other every time they meet. Many do not use personal names as freely as non-Aboriginal people and often address each other by kinship terms. Some find constant eye contact uncomfortable. It is good manners not to photograph Bininj/Mungguy without permission, to listen carefully and think before answering, and to say goodbye when leaving; their word for goodbye is 'bobo' (pronounced bor bor).
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Do not enter restricted areas. They may be sacred sites, ceremonial sites, burial grounds or someone's home.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Aboriginal Traditional Owners of Kakadu, jointly managing the park with Parks Australia.
